root_cause.text: In crypto/seqiv.c, seqiv_aead_encrypt() performed a post-encryption comparison against req->iv even though crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq) can complete asynchronously and free the underlying aead_request, causing a use-after-free of the request structure.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “As soon as crypto_aead_encrypt is called, the underlying request may be freed by an asynchronous completion. Thus dereferencing req->iv after it returns is invalid,” and the patch removes the post-call check `if (unlikely(info != req->iv))` in favor of a precomputed `bool unaligned_info`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states “As soon as crypto_aead_encrypt is called, the underlying request may be freed by an asynchronous completion. intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local flag in seqiv_aead_encrypt() to support upcoming handling of unaligned info buffer state.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable named unaligned_info was added to the seqiv_aead_encrypt() function declaration list.
intent_record.how: This introduces storage for tracking whether the info buffer is unaligned, enabling subsequent logic in the function to handle alignment-sensitive behavior during encryption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cache the IV alignment check result in `unaligned_info` so the code can reuse the unaligned state without recomputing it.
intent_record.what: The alignment check on `info` was split out by assigning the result of `!IS_ALIGNED((unsigned long)info, crypto_aead_alignmask(geniv) + 1)` to a new `unaligned_info` variable, and the subsequent `if (unlikely(...))` condition was changed to test `unlikely(unaligned_info)` instead of recomputing the expression inline.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this stores whether `info` is unaligned in a variable before the conditional branch, so the later code can reuse that exact alignment status instead of recalculating it; this preserves the existing branch behavior while making the unaligned state explicitly available for subsequent logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the explicit unaligned-info condition to invoke completion handling after AEAD encryption instead of relying on pointer comparison.
intent_record.what: The post-encryption condition in seqiv_aead_encrypt() was changed from checking whether `info != req->iv` to checking the boolean `unaligned_info` before calling `seqiv_aead_encrypt_complete2(req, err)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the cleanup/completion helper is now triggered based on whether the IV/info buffer was identified as unaligned rather than based on pointer inequality, making the follow-up handling depend on alignment state instead of raw address comparison.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a local flag for future unaligned info buffer handling and does not address the post-encryption req->iv access or the asynchronous use-after-free in seqiv_aead_encrypt().

The change only caches the IV alignment/unaligned state for reuse. It does not address the post-encryption comparison against req->iv, asynchronous completion, or the resulting use-after-free of the aead_request.

The root cause is the unsafe post-encryption pointer comparison against req->iv after an asynchronous AEAD call may have freed the request. This change replaces that pointer-based post-call check with an explicit unaligned-info condition for deciding completion handling, directly addressing the use-after-free trigger.

candidates.rationale: This post-encryption comparison dereferences req after crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq) returns, even though the operation may complete asynchronously and free the underlying aead_request, making req a potential use-after-free.
This call can complete asynchronously and trigger freeing of the underlying request, creating the unsafe condition for the subsequent access to req in the pointer comparison.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs a post-encryption access to req->iv after crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq) may have completed asynchronously and freed the underlying aead_request, directly causing the use-after-free.
This call is the enabling operation because it may complete asynchronously and free the underlying request, making the following dereference of req in the pointer comparison unsafe.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the full AEAD encrypt path introduced by this commit, including the post-encryption handling around `crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq)`. The vulnerable construct is present in both `seqiv_aead_encrypt_compat()` and `seqiv_aead_encrypt()`: after calling `err = crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq);`, the code immediately checks `if (unlikely(info != req->iv)) seqiv_aead_encrypt_complete2(req, err);`. The root cause says the bug occurs because `crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq)` may complete asynchronously and free the underlying `aead_request`, so any post-call use of request-backed state is unsafe. Here, `seqiv_aead_encrypt_complete2()` does `struct aead_request *subreq = aead_request_ctx(req);` and then accesses `subreq->iv` via `memcpy(req->iv, subreq->iv, crypto_aead_ivsize(geniv));` and finally `kzfree(subreq->iv);`. Since this helper is invoked after `crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq)` returns, it can run when `err == -EINPROGRESS`, i.e. asynchronous completion, and thus may touch `subreq` after the lower layer has taken ownership/completed asynchronously. Although `seqiv_aead_encrypt_complete2()` returns early on `-EINPROGRESS`, the buggy pattern is still the post-encryption comparison and callback-time/manual completion split based on `if (unlikely(info != req->iv))` after the encrypt call, exactly the construct described in the root cause. There is no fix here that eliminates this post-encryption check/cleanup path before the async completion callback; instead the code still performs the comparison and may call the helper after `crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq)`. Therefore the function contains the vulnerable construct and is not yet fixed.

Author: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
Date:   Wed Dec 12 12:27:26 2007 +0800

    [CRYPTO] seqiv: Add AEAD support
    
    This patch adds support for using seqiv with AEAD algorithms.  This is
    useful for those AEAD algorithms that performs authentication before
    encryption because the IV generated by the underlying encryption algorithm
    won't be available for authentication.
    
    Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.
bic_trace_step.reason: The added AEAD path clearly contains the vulnerable post-encryption handling. In `seqiv_aead_givencrypt()`, after `err = crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq);`, the code does `if (unlikely(info != areq->iv)) seqiv_aead_complete2(req, err);`. The root cause is that `crypto_aead_encrypt(subreq)` may complete asynchronously, so `subreq`/request memory may no longer be safe to access after this call returns. Yet `seqiv_aead_complete2()` immediately dereferences the request context: `struct aead_request *subreq = aead_givcrypt_reqctx(req);` and then, on success, copies from `subreq->iv` via `memcpy(req->areq.iv, subreq->iv, crypto_aead_ivsize(geniv));`, and finally frees `subreq->iv` with `kfree(subreq->iv);`. This is exactly the unsafe post-encryption access pattern described in the root cause. There is no protective check that limits this post-call handling to synchronous completion only; specifically, the call site invokes `seqiv_aead_complete2(req, err)` whenever `info != areq->iv`, regardless of whether `err` indicates asynchronous progress. Although `seqiv_aead_complete2()` returns early for `err == -EINPROGRESS`, the vulnerable construct is still present because the post-encryption comparison/handling against request-owned state occurs after an operation that may complete asynchronously. Therefore this commit introduces the bug and does not contain the fix.
